Enable Banking Changelog | October 2026
Enable Banking September 2026 Changelog
This month there’s a change to how we support personal-use applications. On the integration side, most major French banks now return account holder names, Italian banks offer transaction history beyond 90 days, and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer is live at a long list of French and Belgian banks.
Significant Changes and Updates
Swedbank: BankID Login Fixed for Customers of Multiple Banks

Restricted applications let anyone build with Enable Banking using their own bank accounts for personal use. We’ve kept this option open on purpose, because we want to support side projects and people experimenting with new ideas. We love seeing what people are building with our infrastructure.

Over the past months, the number of people using restricted applications has grown significantly. AI tools have made it much easier to build your own application, even without a background in software development. Our CMO built her first application with Claude, and plenty of others are exploring what is possible.

It’s great to see. More people can experiment, build and work with financial data than ever before. To keep giving our partners the support they rely on, we’ve changed how we handle support requests.

Since late October 2026, support works as follows:
Partners and companies in a trial or evaluation with our team continue to get support from our team, as before. If you’re already in touch with us about working together, nothing changes for you. 
Restricted applications used for personal purposes are supported by our AI assistant. Email support.api@enablebanking.com as usual, and the assistant will reply. It answers from our docs, knowledge base, and code samples, and is there to help with questions it can answer.
This lets our team focus on hands-on support for partners and companies preparing to work with us, while making technical guidance easier to reach for everyone building with us.

We can’t wait to see what you build next.

Account Holder Names from French Banks

Many French banks now return the account holder's name in the "AccountResource name" property. These include BNP Paribas, Hello bank!, Banque Populaire & Caisse d'Epargne banks, La Banque Postale, Société Générale, and Arkéa banks such as Crédit Mutuel de Bretagne, Fortuneo and AXA Banque.

This makes it possible to check who owns an account, for example, to match it against your own customer data. For joint accounts, all holders are listed when the bank provides them.

Why the name is sometimes missing

Holder names are optional under the French STET standard, and banks expose them differently. Most of the banks above return the holders of each account. Société Générale only provides the identity of the person who logged in, so a joint account shows only that person. Some banks return no holder information for certain accounts or account types.

We handle these differences on our side, so your integration works the same way across banks. When the bank gives us no name, the name is then "null".
Transaction History Beyond 90 Days in Italy

Most integrations towards Italian banks using CBI Globe to provide Open Banking APIs now support consent extension for access to historic transactions over 90 days old. These include Intesa Sanpaolo, BancoPosta, Monte dei Paschi, Banco BPM, BNL, BPER, Credem, Crédit Agricole Italia, Raiffeisen Südtirol, Nexi and the Allitude banks.

Previously, transaction history from these banks was limited to 90 days. We now request the extended consent automatically during authorisation, so that your application receives as much history beyond the 90 days as the bank makes available. That’s how it already works with many banks, so you don’t need to change anything in your integration to get it.

The difference is that these banks ask for an additional Strong Customer Authentication before sharing the older transactions. In practice, your end users may have to authenticate twice when connecting an account. Italy isn’t the only market that works this way. Swedbank, Luminor, Artea and Šiaulių bankas, among others, also require an extra SCA for history beyond 90 days.
Control Panel Updates: Multi-Factor Authentication Changes and Account Deletion
Authenticator App Support for MFA
You can now secure your Control Panel account with time-based authenticator apps, such as Google Authenticator, 1Password, or Authy.

To set it up, go to your profile page and click “Enable” next to the Authenticator app. Scan the QR code or enter the setup key manually, then type in the 6-digit code shown in your app. You’ll be signed out and prompted to sign in again using a code from your app. Once MFA is enabled, it can’t be turned off again from your account.

Enabling MFA is a sensitive operation, so it requires a recent authentication session. If enabling MFA fails, clicking “Try again” won’t fix it. Instead, sign out of the Control Panel, sign back in, and enable MFA from your profile straight away.

SMS verification codes are no longer available for new MFA setups. If you already use SMS-based MFA, it keeps working as before. If you have both SMS and an authenticator app enabled, the Control Panel asks for your app code first, with a “Send a code by SMS instead” option below the input field.
Self-Service Account Deletion

You can now delete your Control Panel account yourself, without contacting us. On your profile page, click “Delete account” next to your email address, type your email address to confirm, and press “Delete account”. For security reasons, this also requires a recent sign-in. If it isn’t working, try signing out and back in, and then try again.


Deleting your account:
Permanently removes your account data, including your email address, full name, phone number, Mock ASPSP data, and identifiers of accounts linked to production applications
Deactivates your applications, except applications shared with other users, which stay active and accessible to those users
Cancels your subscriptions to ASPSP availability notifications
Account deletion can’t be undone. If you sign in with the same email address afterwards, a new, empty account is created.
Deleting your Control Panel account doesn’t unsubscribe you from our changelog emails. To stop receiving them, use the Unsubscribe link at the bottom of any changelog email.

# Moneo Moneo is an open-source personal finance app that runs on your own computer. Import bank statements or sync your bank, track accounts and wealth, plan spending, and ask questions about your money in chat or on a voice call. Figures always come from your own records; the AI explains them and suggests changes that you accept. Website: **[indkhan.github.io/Moneo](https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/)** — screenshots, what Moneo does, and the right installer for your computer. Everything stays on your computer. There are no accounts and no sign-in screen: one owner, one workspace. The only data that leaves your computer goes to the services you connect (your AI provider, and optionally your bank or Scalable Capital). ## Install ### Desktop preview Desktop installers for Windows, macOS and Linux are attached to [GitHub releases](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/releases) once published (none is published yet; until then, use the source installation below): download, install and open Moneo; nothing else is needed. Settings → App updates installs newer releases and keeps your data. See [desktop setup and operation](desktop/README.md) for packaging, data locations, backups and signing requirements. The desktop app bundles its local backend and does not require Docker or Node.js. The source installation below remains supported. Scalable questions in chat and voice can combine live holdings, paginated transaction history and transaction details with local JavaScript calculations. The calculation sandbox has no network, filesystem or credentials. Read results remain subject to your AI data scopes and are sent to your configured AI provider as needed to answer. Trades still require accepting an approval card. No additional setup is needed. ### Easiest: let an AI agent install it If you use an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, it can do the install for you with the `moneo-setup` skill that comes with Moneo. Open the agent in an empty folder and paste: > Clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo, then set it up by following .agents/skills/moneo-setup/SKILL.md in that repository. If you already downloaded Moneo, open the agent in the Moneo folder and say **"set up Moneo"**. The agent runs the commands, tells you what each step does, and asks you only for what it can't do itself, like installing Docker or entering your keys in Moneo. If it can control your browser or computer, it asks first and then does the clicking too. You type passwords and keys yourself. ### Or install it yourself #### 1. Install the tools - [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads) - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) version 22 or newer - [Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) (on Linux, Docker Engine with Compose) Start Docker Desktop and wait until it says it is running. #### 2. Download Moneo ```sh git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git cd Moneo npm ci ``` #### 3. Run the setup ```sh npm run setup ``` This creates the database in Docker, makes all the passwords and secrets Moneo needs, and saves them in a file called `.env`. The first run downloads a few GB and takes several minutes; you need about 4 GB of free disk space. On Windows a security prompt may ask to install a local certificate: click **Yes** (it is only used for bank connections and only trusted on this computer). You never need to open or edit `.env`. Keep it private and don't delete it. #### 4. Start Moneo ```sh npm run build npm start ``` The build takes a few minutes the first time. Then open **http://localhost:3000**. #### 5. Turn on the AI Go to **Settings → Keys and connections → AI access** and choose one: - **Sign in with ChatGPT** to use your ChatGPT Go, Plus or Pro plan, - **Sign in with Claude** to use your Claude Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan (see [Use your Claude plan](#use-your-claude-plan-optional)), or - **Paste an OpenAI API key** ([create one here](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)) and click **Save key**. Usage is billed to that key. Voice calls and dictation need the OpenAI API key. An OpenRouter key is optional (for other models). #### 6. Add your money - **Import** a CSV or Excel export from your bank, or - connect your bank or Scalable Capital (optional, see below). That's it. Want it on your phone or tablet too? See [Use it from your phone or tablet](#use-it-from-your-phone-or-tablet-optional). ## Everyday use - **Start Moneo:** `npm start` in the Moneo folder (Docker Desktop must be running). - **Stop Moneo:** press `Ctrl+C`. The database keeps running in Docker; `docker compose stop` stops it. - **Update Moneo:** ```sh git pull npm ci npm run setup npm run build npm start ``` Your data and secrets are kept. While Moneo runs it does its background work by itself: scheduled summaries, and syncing your bank and Scalable about once a day. Anything missed while your computer was off runs shortly after you start Moneo. Opening Moneo or coming back to it also syncs in the background (Scalable at most every 15 minutes, banks at most every hour): you see the last numbers right away and the page updates when the sync lands. If a value can't be refreshed, it still counts in your net worth and Wealth marks it as not from today. A short message in the corner of Home tells you once about old values and about a connection that failed or needs reconnecting. ## Keys and connections Every key and outside service is set up in the app under **Settings → Keys and connections**. Keys are checked with the provider before they are saved, stored encrypted in your database, shown only by their last four characters, and can be replaced or removed at any time. The same section shows that the secrets made by `npm run setup` are in place. ### Use your Claude plan (optional) Moneo can run on your Claude subscription instead of an API key. It uses Claude Code, which comes with Moneo, signed in with your own Claude account on this computer. Moneo never sees or stores your Claude login; Claude Code keeps it, the same one the Claude Code app uses. 1. In **Settings → AI access**, click **Sign in with Claude** on this computer. A Claude sign-in page opens in your browser. 2. Sign in. If the page shows a code, paste it into Moneo and click **Continue**. If you're already signed in to Claude Code, Moneo shows your account straight away; click **Use Claude plan**. Chat, artifacts, briefings, imports and the agents then run on Claude (Opus 5.5 for the chat, Haiku 5.5 for lighter tasks; change them under **Settings → AI and your data → Advanced**). Requests count toward your plan's usage limits, shown at [claude.ai/settings/usage](https://claude.ai/settings/usage). - **Never billed to an API key.** Moneo removes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and similar settings before it starts Claude Code, and only runs Claude when Claude Code is signed in with a Claude plan. If you sign out of Claude Code, AI stays off until you sign in again or pick another option. - **Only Moneo's tools.** Claude gets Moneo's finance tools and nothing else: no files, no shell, no other MCP servers, and no chat history saved by Claude Code. Changes still go through cards you accept. - **PDFs in chat** are read on your computer and sent to Claude as text. A scanned PDF has no text to read, so attach photos of its pages instead. - **Not yet:** voice calls and dictation, which still need an OpenAI API key for the audio. - **Stop using Claude** switches Moneo back to ChatGPT or your API key. It doesn't sign you out of Claude Code. - Anthropic's rules say apps may not offer Claude plan sign-in without its approval ([Agent SDK overview](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview)). Moneo only uses the Claude Code login you set up yourself, on your own computer. Decide for yourself whether that fits your use. ### Connect your bank (optional) Moneo syncs booked transactions and balances from EU banks (for example Revolut and Commerzbank) through [Enable Banking](https://enablebanking.com). It is free for personal use. Each sync is an ordinary import that you can review and undo. 1. Sign up at the [Enable Banking control panel](https://enablebanking.com/cp/) and create an application in the **Production** environment. 2. Fill in the application form: - Redirect URL: `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` - Privacy policy URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/privacy.html` - Terms of service URL: `https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/terms.html` 3. Let the control panel make the key pair, and keep the downloaded private key file (`.pem`). 4. In the control panel, link your own bank accounts to the application. Only linked accounts can be synced. 5. In Moneo, go to **Settings → Keys and connections → Connected banks** (also on the Import page). Paste the application ID, paste the private key or upload the `.pem` file, and click **Save and check**. 6. Click **Choose a bank**, pick yours, click **Connect bank** and approve access at your bank. Bank consent usually lasts up to 180 days; Moneo shows a reconnect banner 7 days before it ends. Pending transactions are not synced. If Enable Banking says it rejected the return address, add the Redirect URL from step 2 to your application and try again. ### Connect Scalable Capital (optional) 1. In Scalable on the web, go to **Profile → Security → Agentic Investing** and turn on access (read-only is enough). 2. In Moneo, click **Connect Scalable Capital** under **Settings → Keys and connections** (also on the Import page) and log in to Scalable (with 2FA in the Scalable app). Moneo then reads your holdings, totals and cash every day and shows the portfolio on Wealth. No keys are needed. It also keeps Scalable's own record of your deposits and withdrawals, read in full once after connecting, so money moving between your bank and Scalable counts once on every day of the net worth chart, and a withdrawal that bounced back looks as if the money stayed. Soon after the first sync, a background job works out your portfolio's past value from your Scalable transactions and past prices, so its chart reaches back to your first trade and connecting a portfolio doesn't look like a gain in net worth. Those days are an estimate, saved apart from your real records: prices further than a year back are monthly. Moneo only saves them if replaying your transactions lands on the shares and cash you hold today; otherwise the chart simply starts at your first sync, and it tries again the next day. Disconnecting keeps them, like your synced values, and resetting all data clears them. Artifact Pages and Home cards can show your Scalable portfolio, recent activity and watchlist. By default they use the last sync, the same figures as Wealth. Turn on **Live Scalable data in artifacts** in Settings → AI and your data to read Scalable each time one opens; that also allows quotes, charts and news for any security, but loads slower and needs Scalable to be reachable. ### Use it from your phone or tablet (optional) Your phone becomes another screen on the Moneo running on this computer: same data, same ChatGPT, Claude, bank and Scalable connections. It is off until you turn it on, and nothing changes on this computer. 1. Go to **Settings → Keys and connections → Phone and tablet** and click **Turn on**. Moneo tells you if it needs [Tailscale](https://tailscale.com/download) installed, a sign-in, or one approval for secure addresses. 2. On your phone or tablet, install Tailscale and sign in with the same account. 3. Scan the code in Settings, then choose **Add to Home Screen**. The address and code are your own, from your own Tailscale account. Only devices on your Tailscale network can reach Moneo, and they get in without a password, so don't use a network you share with other people. Leave Tailscale Funnel off: Moneo refuses traffic from the public internet. Moneo then opens like an app. It never keeps your numbers on the phone: when the computer is off, it says so and shows nothing until the computer is back. Keep this computer on and awake with Moneo running: on a laptop, stay plugged in and set closing the lid to do nothing. After a restart, start Docker and run `npm start` again. On Windows, `tailscale set --unattended=true` keeps Tailscale connected after a restart. New ChatGPT, Claude, bank and Scalable logins start on this computer, because those services only return to its address. On Linux, first run `sudo tailscale set --operator=$USER`. # Moneo Desktop

An Electron app that runs Moneo with its own private database on the owner's computer: no Docker,
Node.js, terminal or `.env`. The source setup (`npm run setup`, `npm run dev`) is unchanged.

## Build

```sh
node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform win-x64   # native backend + mkcert → desktop/.build (see that script)
npm run desktop:build                    # Next.js standalone server + migrations → desktop/.build, main process → desktop/dist
npm run desktop:dev                      # run Electron on the unpacked build
npm run desktop:dist                     # installers → desktop/release (Windows NSIS, macOS dmg+zip, Linux AppImage+deb)
npm run desktop:smoke                    # drive the packaged app (desktop/release/*-unpacked) end to end
```

`desktop:build` runs `next build` with `MONEO_DESKTOP_BUILD=1` (standalone output in `.next-desktop/`, so
`.next` is untouched) and every `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable unset. It refuses to run when a `.env*` file
in the checkout sets `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` (Next.js would bake those addresses in), and fails if a local
Supabase address ends up in the output anyway.

Packages are unsigned by default. With `CSC_LINK` and `CSC_KEY_PASSWORD` set, electron-builder signs;
on macOS `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_APP_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD` and `APPLE_TEAM_ID` also notarize. Unsigned macOS
builds get an ad-hoc signature. Package each platform on that platform (`npm run desktop:dist -- --win`,
`--mac`, `--linux`); the macOS and Linux backend needs a native addon built there.

## Where things live

- Package: `app.asar` holds only `dist/`, `setup/` and the icon. Next to it: `app/` (Next server),
  `migrations/`, `bootstrap/`, `backend/<os>-<arch>/`, `storage-api/`.
- Per user: the Electron user-data folder (`MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` overrides it): `config.json` (backend
  secrets), `shell.json` (app port, tray notice, last backup), `postgres/`, `storage/`, `data/`
  (ChatGPT sign-in, bank certificate), `backups/`, `logs/`, `chromium/` (the window's own cookies).

The app listens on `http://localhost:47300` (chosen once, then kept: phone access, Scalable's return
address and ChatGPT's callback name it). If it is taken on the first run, a free port is saved instead.

## Behaviour

- Start: a small status window shows each step (the first run says it is creating a private database),
  then the app window opens Home. On failure it offers Try again, Open logs folder, Restore from backup, Quit.
- Closing the window keeps Moneo in the tray, so background syncs and phone access keep working.
  Quit (tray, Cmd+Q, `Moneo --quit`, OS shutdown) stops the server, then the database, then exits.
- Daily automatic backup while running; Back up now, Open backups folder and Restore from backup in the tray.
- Sign-ins (ChatGPT, banks, Scalable) open in the system browser and return to Moneo's loopback
  callbacks. The callback then opens its result (Import or Settings) in the app window and brings it
  to the front; the browser tab says to continue in Moneo. The server reaches the window through a
  loopback address that is random for each launch and refuses browser requests (`src/bridge.ts`);
  if the window cannot take it, the browser shows the result as in a source checkout. Every other address also goes to the browser
  (https only). The window allows only the microphone and copying, for Moneo's own pages.
- Updates: Settings → App updates checks the newest published GitHub release only when the owner
  asks (`src/updates.ts`, electron-updater). On Windows and with the AppImage, Update downloads it,
  quits Moneo cleanly, installs it and starts Moneo again; data stays in the user folder, and a pending
  migration makes a `pre-upgrade` backup first. macOS (unsigned) and `.deb` installs open the release
  page to download instead. Draft and pre-releases are never offered. `npm run desktop:dist` writes
  the `latest*.yml` files the check reads; the release workflow uploads them with the installers.

## Releasing

Releases are made only from a `v*` tag; pull request runs keep their installers as workflow
artifacts for 7 days and never create a release.

1. Bump `desktop/package.json`'s version on `main` (the first release is `0.1.0` as is).
2. Tag and push: `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`.
3. The Desktop workflow builds every platform and drafts a release with the installers, `latest*.yml`,
   blockmaps and `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
4. Publish the draft on GitHub. Drafts are invisible to visitors, to the landing page's download
   button and to Settings → App updates; once published, all three offer it.

### Bank return certificate

Enable Banking returns to `https://localhost:3443`. On every start Moneo makes that certificate with the
bundled mkcert if it is missing (its signing authority lives in the user folder, `mkcert/`); nothing is
trusted yet. The first time the owner opens a bank's consent page, Moneo explains why and asks the
computer to trust that authority once: Windows shows its own confirmation (current user's store),
macOS asks for the login keychain password, Linux adds it to the browsers' NSS store (needs `certutil`).

## Security fuses

For a private copied-data preview, launch the desktop executable with `MONEO_DESKTOP_PREVIEW=1`.
This runtime-only flag prevents persisted Workflow recovery, the scheduler and the bank callback
listener from starting, and skips automatic bank/Scalable sync when opening a page. It does not
block network requests triggered by explicit actions in the app, and is
not an offline mode. Normal desktop launches and source development keep their usual behavior.

RunAsNode, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `--inspect` are off; cookie encryption, asar-only loading and embedded asar
integrity are on. The smoke test reads them back from the packaged executable. Because `--inspect` is off,
Playwright's `_electron.launch` cannot attach, so the smoke test drives the app over
`--remote-debugging-port` instead. DevTools are off in packaged builds unless `MONEO_DESKTOP_DEBUG=1`.

PR #214 is open: https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/214. The v0.1.2 release isn't out yet: its Mac builds are being re-run now, and I'll publish the release if they pass.

**What I did as a new user:** I downloaded the Windows installer from the landing page and its checksum matched. I ran the released v0.1.1 app with its own data folder, so your Moneo wasn't touched. I turned on AI with your Claude plan, imported a sample bank CSV, and the agent team then ran by itself. That basic path works.

**What the PR fixes:**
1. **Mac downloads:** the latest release (v0.1.1) has no Mac installer, but the Mac buttons on the landing page led to a release page without one. They now say "Not in this release yet" and point to running from source.
2. **README:** it still said no release was published. It now starts with the download.
3. **Settings in the desktop app:** it told people to run `npm run setup` and use a `.env` file, neither of which exists in the app. That text now only shows for source installs.
4. **Bank country list:** only 11 countries were listed, as two-letter codes, so people in Sweden, Poland, Norway and other countries couldn't find their bank. It now lists all 29 countries Enable Banking serves, by name, and starts on the user's own country.
5. **Enable Banking setup:** the instructions were one dense sentence. They're now five numbered steps that say the setup is free and takes about 10 minutes.
6. **Landing page FAQ and steps:** they now say any bank works through statement import, and that bank sync is an optional one-time setup.

**From the Enable Banking changelog:** two items were useful. Moneo now warns that some banks ask you to approve twice (for example in Italy, where it's needed for history older than 90 days). The README also gives their new support address for personal-use apps, where an AI assistant answers. The new banks in Sweden, Norway and Denmark only became reachable through fix 4. The other changelog items don't affect Moneo.

**Checks:** lint and typecheck pass. In the full unit test run, 1560 passed and two failed on timeouts, in files this PR doesn't touch; both pass when run alone. Nothing here overlaps the open PRs #204–#211.

**Mac release:** the v0.1.2 tag already existed. Its build failed on both Macs because Apple's signing check (`codesign`) rejected the app: "invalid destination for symbolic link in bundle". A pull request build made after the same Mac fix passed on both Macs, so I think the failure came from a stale build cache, but I haven't confirmed that. If the re-run fails again, there's a real bundling bug to fix first, and I'll ask you before going further.

I didn't test phone access or connect a real bank or Scalable, because those would touch your own accounts.

Not released yet: I've found the cause of the Mac failures and a second bug that blocks any release, and both fixes are in PR #215 (https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/215). Its full Desktop build is running now.

- **Mac builds:** the bundled Next.js server kept package links that pointed by absolute path into the build machine's checkout, outside the app. Apple's signing check rejects that. On the first CI run, after the build copied those links in, both Mac apps signed and passed the check. PR builds now also sign Macs, so a problem like this shows up on a PR instead of on a release tag.
- **Restore from backup:** this is broken in the desktop app on main since #212 merged; a CI check had already caught it before #212 merged. #212 added a database role, `moneo_reader`, that backups don't include, so restoring stopped on every platform. The setup that restore runs first now creates that role. #215's description also suggests one rule for AGENTS.md: any migration that creates a role must add it there too.

Your first-run fixes in #214 are merged.

**Next:** if this build passes, merge #215 (I won't merge without your go-ahead). Then I'll bump the version to 0.1.3, tag it and publish the release with Windows, Mac and Linux installers. I'd rather not move the `v0.1.2` tag, because it's already on GitHub pointing at the broken commit. Tell me if you'd prefer otherwise.

The fix for the last CI failure is pushed to PR #215 (https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/215). CI is running it on all four platforms now, so no release yet.

The last round failed because of my earlier restore fix. I had the app's database setup create the `moneo_reader` role, which made the setup account its owner. The data_query migration then wasn't allowed to grant that role. The setup now gives the migration permission to manage the role, the same way the other built-in roles are set up. I checked this on a throwaway database using the PostgreSQL bundled in the downloaded app: the old version gives the same error as CI, and the new one runs.

If CI passes, #215 is ready for you to merge. After that I'll bump the version to 0.1.3, tag it and publish the release with the Mac installers. If CI fails, I'll fix it and run it again.
